descriptionChirho: Feminine demonstrative pronoun 'this,' pointing to a specific entity, situation, or referent in the immediate discourse context. Translated as English 'this,' Spanish 'esto/esta,' Hindi 'yah/joh' (यह/जोह), Arabic 'hadhihi' (هٰذِهِ), Korean 'igeot' (이것), Swahili 'hii/hili.' This is the bare demonstrative function without prepositional modification, used nine times in the Hebrew Bible as an archaic feminine form parallel to masculine zeh.

labelChirho: thus, in this manner (with preposition ke)
descriptionChirho: The demonstrative zoh combined with preposition ke- to form an adverbial expression meaning 'thus, in this manner, like this, so.' Translated as English 'thus/like this,' Spanish 'asi,' Hindi 'aisa' (ऐसा), Arabic 'kadha/kahadha' (كَذَا/كَهٰذا), Korean 'ireoke/igachi' (이렇게/이같이), Swahili 'hivi.' Both clusters represent the same prepositional+demonstrative construction with identical adverbial function, differing only slightly in contextual nuance.
